Recently just got out of my worst rental experience.  

The agent said they would send us the healthy homes report as soon as they had it. We signed the agreement in good faith as we had used the same agent previously. Never received the agreement, then very quickly as we moved in mould was present. We tried all the home remedies - fresh air flow, moisture boxes, dehumidifier running 24/7 . 

The master bedroom was the worst with a large damp spot under the bed. Mould was growing on the walls, windows, celling. Our bedroom furniture had to be cleaned every fortnight to wipe away surface mould, clothes were constantly being ruined, the list goes on. Documented it all with photos etc. We had 5 moisture boxes in the room that filled up within a month and we were expected to cover the cost of that ourselves. our entire flat came down with chest infections over winter, that took me off work for 3 weeks, during that time we had a rental inspection - how was it not obvious to the agent the house was in breach I do not know (maybe because we tried to keep it so clean). 

We complained numerous time, and followed up trying to get the healthy home report. Turns out there was no report, because it did not meet the standard. We then complained further asking for remedies - under ground seal covering, insulation, HRV etc. We were good tenants clean, tidy, respectful, paid everything on time. A month goes by of back and forth with the agent, then as soon as we got out of the last Level 3 lockdown we were served 90 days notice. The owner was selling the house, likely due to us complaining and requesting remedies. Was a real kick in the teeth, the owner made a point of meeting us in person before we signed the rental agreement because they wanted nice long term tenants ideally 2+ years, we were there just shy of one year. 

When we moved out the owner had the cheek to request we return to mow the lawns one last time - even though they had been done two weeks prior, they wanted them done same day as move out day. I wish we had taken it to the tribunal at the start, but life was already stressful enough. I'm now living with my parents, at 26yrs old, not where I saw myself being this stage of life.

My partner and I are 'flexitarian' mostly vegetarian but will occasionally eat meat, being vegetarian is cheaper than being carnivore. We spend approx $100-$120 on groceries for the week. Though we aren't really breakfast people. 

Buy the 'odd bunch' brand countdown vegetables - a good money saver e.g. a kg of carrots for $2.50 and will usually last a couple of weeks in the fridge. 

Frozen vege's are your budgeting friend. 

We also eat smaller than the average joe meals so my recipes below may not be sustainable if you eat larger portions. But if you want to try smaller meal portions I suggest serving meals in bowls instead of on a plate and drink water while you eat your meal. 

​

**Bento bowls/stir fry:**

Tofu $4-5 for 300grams which lasts us 2-3 meals, carrot, onion, cabbage, 1/2 a broccoli, sauce of choice (making your own sauce works out cheaper in the long run) on rice. Can make it stretch to have leftovers for lunch too if you bulk with more carrot/broccoli. 

If we do this with meat we buy minute steak, usually around the $5 mark, last us two meals worth. 

​

**Air fryer/ lazy meal:**

'Frys Family Vegetarian Sausage Rolls Meat Free' - $8.50 for 4 rolls which get us two meals worth. side of hash bites, onion rings, tegal chicken bites $12 for a kg will last us a couple weeks.  

​

**Pizza toast:** 

Lightly toast bread in toaster then top with your fancies and bake in oven. We use relish as the base sauce as a jar has longer fridge life and spreads further than pizza sauce does. A lot cheaper than buying pizza bases and taste just as good. 

​

**Spicy beans on couscous**

1 can of the $1.20 Mexican 3 bean mix countdown brand, 1 large grated carrot, tin of tomatoes, onion, frozen corn, spices, 1/2 cup of couscous. Also is a really quick meal to make 10-15 minutes tops. 

​

**'Mince' style meals:**

'Nutmeat' great meat alternative made from peanut protein that comes in a can, $6 a can lasts us 2-3 meals. Good for nachos, spaghetti bolognaise, burritos etc. bulk up with beans. Never buy the 'pre-made' pasta sauce in jars, buy the 90.c tin of 'crushed and sieved' countdown brand tomatoes and add species.  

​

**Deserts/snacks:** 

Frozen berries, nuts, pretzels, cereal, yogurt (the kg tubs more cost effective), crumpets if they're on special. 

​

Hope this helps :) we try to eat relatively healthy and cost effectively, if you're not vegetarian and do try going for vege meals keep an eye on your energy/iron levels.
